content: The mammary souffle is a type of heart murmur that is typically heard during the later stages of pregnancy and the early postpartum period in women who are lactating. This murmur is believed to originate from arterial blood flow and may occur on both sides of the chest (bilaterally). On physical examination, the mammary souffle can present as a continuous murmur. It becomes louder and peaks during systole (the phase of the heartbeat when the heart contracts and pumps blood). The murmur disappears when the patient assumes an upright position and can be completely eliminated by applying local compression to the area.
